title: Frontier I: Problem L is zero-sum subset search (~r); isogeny cannot reach weak curves
question: Frontier I (ECDLP-60, last literature long shots): both dead. (1) Mahalanobis-Mallick Problem L (2017 arXiv 1703.07544v3 read in full; 2026 follow-up abstract, sec 1.1, sec 5): reduction is exactly a zero-sum-subset search (3n-subset of N=3n+l random multiples of P and -Q summing to O <=> singular l x l kernel-matrix minor), verified on 50,488 subsets over 4 toy curves with 0 exceptions; Algorithm 2 per-pass success c l^2/r (c ~ 2.5, flat over r 190-29,000), total ~2.4 r group operations; exhaustive Problem L fit beta 0.94 [0.82,1.0]; generic MITM subset-sum alpha ~3.5 sqrt r vs rho control ~3.0 sqrt r; follow-up paper Table 2 itself reports exponent ~1. (2) Isogeny distance to weak curves: order, trace, embedding degree, anomalous, supersingular are isogeny-invariant (380 Velu 2-isogeny steps: order never changed, dlog transported 380/380), so distance is 0 or infinite; j=0/1728 reachable only if CM field Q(sqrt-3)/Q(i), class fraction ~2.5/sqrt p (beta -0.49 [-0.55,-0.43], 32 primes up to 1.07e6), gain at most sqrt 6; every curve in a class has non-scalar endomorphisms of degree >= |d_K|/4.
rationale: Remaining untested routes named by the round-17 literature survey.
